what: The Roman Numeral Converter changes normal numbers into Roman numerals and Roman numerals back into numbers. It has two boxes; type in either one and the other updates right away. It supports whole numbers from 1 to 3999.

It is useful for reading dates on buildings and film credits, writing years for tattoos, invitations or clock faces, checking school homework, and understanding chapter or event numbers like Super Bowl LX. It also checks that a numeral is written correctly.
The conversion runs in your browser as you type.
uses: Turn a birth year, wedding year or founding year into Roman numerals.
Understand dates carved on buildings or shown in film credits.
Make sure a Roman numeral answer is correct.
Get the right numerals for chapters, sections or events.
Find out if a numeral like IIII or IC is a valid standard form.
tutorial: Enter a whole number from 1 to 3999 in "Number (1 to 3999)". The Roman numeral appears in the other box at once.
Enter letters in "Roman numeral", using I, V, X, L, C, D and M. Lowercase is fine; it is shown in capitals. The number appears in the first box.
Below the boxes, a short line gives help. If the input is not valid, it explains why, for example "Roman numerals cover whole numbers from 1 to 3999."
Empty either box and the other one clears too.
features: The tool takes the largest value it can from this list each time: M 1000, CM 900, D 500, CD 400, C 100, XC 90, L 50, XL 40, X 10, IX 9, V 5, IV 4, I 1.
It reads the letters from left to right using the same list and adds up the values.
A numeral is accepted only if converting it back gives exactly the same letters, so forms like IIII, VX or IC are rejected.
Type in either box; there is no convert button.
Only whole numbers from 1 to 3999 are allowed, with a message if you go outside the range.

example.title: Worked example: 2026 and MCMXCIV
example.text: Type 2026 in the number box. The tool takes M (1000) twice, then X (10) twice, then V (5) and I (1), so the numeral is MMXXVI. Now type MCMXCIV in the Roman numeral box. It reads M = 1000, CM = 900, XC = 90 and IV = 4, and shows 1994. If you type IIII, the message says "IIII" is not a valid Roman numeral, because the standard form of 4 is IV.

tips: Remember the subtractive pairs: IV 4, IX 9, XL 40, XC 90, CD 400, CM 900.
Clock faces sometimes show IIII, but this tool follows the standard form IV.
Spaces at the start or end of a numeral are ignored.
For years above 3999, standard Roman numerals need special overline marks, which this tool does not support.
Type the year first and copy the numeral from the second box.
problems: It says the numeral is not valid
Use only I, V, X, L, C, D and M in standard order. Forms like IIII, VV or IC are not accepted.
You typed 0, a negative number, a decimal or a number above 3999. Enter a whole number in range.
When the input is not valid, the other box is cleared. Fix the input and it fills again.
The box shows letters in capitals. This is normal and does not change the result.
